payload.text: **THE INSTALLED PAIR IS THIS TREE'S BUILD ARTEFACT, SO ANY RELEASE BUILD HERE SWAPS EVERY NODE'S BINARY MID-FLIGHT** (dc measured it 2026-09-17, vc drew the consequence): `~/.local/bin/intent` is a SYMLINK to `native/rust/target/release/intent` in this checkout, so "drive it on the installed pair" and "drive it on this tree's release build" are one run and a copy into a clone is a `cp`. The consequence nobody had written down is that `cargo build --release` in this checkout silently replaces the binary all four nodes are running, with nothing in the tree changing to mark it -- which is the MECHANISM under the rule that no commit lands while a rebuild builds, and it also means a scratch estate that resolves its binary through the symlink can have its subject swapped between an ancestry check and a verdict. A run that must name the version that produced its result pins the resolved file or copies it.
